title: A luminescent linear trinuclear DyIII complex exhibiting slow magnetic relaxation of single ion origin

synthesis.procedure: A mixture of Dy2O3 (0.2 mmol, 0.0746 g), salicylic acid (H2SA, 1.6 mmol, 0.2210 g), 1,10-phenanthroline (phen, 0.4 mmol, 0.0721 g) and distilled H2O (15 mL) was sealed in a 23-mL stainless-steel reactor with a Teflon liner and heated in an oven at 140 °C for 4 days, then cooled to room temperature at 5 °C h−1. Yellow block crystals suitable for X-ray analysis were washed with ethanol–ether and dried in air. The same hydrothermal procedure is given for the Gd analogue using Gd2O3 instead of Dy2O3. The main text only states that 1 and 2 were prepared from Ln2O3 and the organic ligands under hydrothermal conditions, with full quantities in the ESI.

properties.summary: Solid-state photoluminescence of 1 shows ligand-centered emission at 418 nm and DyIII f–f bands at 486 and 580 nm upon excitation at 313 nm. DC susceptibility matches three weakly coupled DyIII ions; reduced magnetization is anisotropic and does not saturate. Zero-field AC susceptibility shows two relaxation regions, with a thermally activated (Orbach) process above 15 K (Arrhenius parameters reported as τ0 = 1.5×10−5 s−1 and ΔE = 65 K) and temperature-independent quantum tunneling below 15 K; no M–H hysteresis is observed at 2 or 4 K. The slow relaxation is assigned to single-ion anisotropy of the three distinct DyIII sites rather than strong exchange.

properties.summary: Under conditions similar to those used for 1, complex 2 shows only a ligand-centered emission at 418 nm; metal-centered GdIII emission is absent because the metal-centered levels lie above the ligand-centered levels. AC susceptibility shows no out-of-phase signal, so the slow relaxation of 1 is not observed for the isotropic GdIII analogue.
